subject: math

entries: Secant lines close in on the tangent - a secant gives an average gradient between two points; slide the points together and the secant becomes the tangent, whose gradient is dy/dx.
slots.label: Secant lines close in on the tangent
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The power rule - differentiate term by term: bring the power down and reduce it by one, so x^3 becomes 3x^2 and x^5 becomes 5x^4, while a constant becomes 0.
slots.label: The power rule
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: dy/dx from first principles - the secant gradient (f(x + h) - f(x)) / h for y = x^2 simplifies to 2x + h, and letting h tend to 0 gives the exact gradient 2x.
slots.label: First principles
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Stationary points: max, min, inflexion - solve dy/dx = 0, then read the sign change of dy/dx either side: positive to negative is a maximum, negative to positive a minimum, no change an inflexion.
slots.label: Stationary points: max, min, inflexion
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Stationary is not always max or min - for y = x^3 the gradient reaches 0 at x = 0 yet stays positive on both sides, so the curve climbs through a point of inflexion.
slots.label: Stationary is not always max or min
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: dy/dx, the gradient function of a curve: it gives the tangent gradient at every point and is found by differentiating.
slots.label: Derivative
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The steepness of a line or curve at a point. For a curve it changes from point to point and equals the gradient of the tangent there.
slots.label: Gradient
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The straight line that just touches a curve at one point and has the same gradient as the curve at that point.
slots.label: Tangent
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A point where dy/dx = 0 and the tangent is horizontal. It may be a maximum, a minimum or a point of inflexion - a sign test decides.
slots.label: Stationary point
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A straight line joining two points on a curve. Its gradient is an average gradient, and it becomes the tangent as the two points close in.
slots.label: Secant
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A point where the curve changes its bending direction. A stationary inflexion, like y = x^3 at x = 0, has dy/dx = 0 but is neither a maximum nor a minimum.
slots.label: Point of inflexion
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: A-Math differentiation: gradients, the power rule and stationary points
